01-industrial-plant.description: Brick industrial building with a loading bay, rooftop equipment, CT cabinet and a small transformer pad.
01-industrial-plant.sizeGuidance: A larger building footprint than a house. Scale CT cabinet and pad separately; a transformer must stay much smaller than the building.

02-utility-depot.description: Two-bay utility depot with a rear crew yard and an AMI communications mast.
02-utility-depot.sizeGuidance: Use the facility footprint. Yard vehicles are separate job-linked assets; do not enlarge or shrink them with the lot polygon.

03-electric-substation.description: Fenced substation yard with a power transformer, switchgear and a control cabinet.
03-electric-substation.sizeGuidance: Calibrate against the fenced facility footprint and explicit supply/feeder connection anchors.

04-water-pump-station.description: Compact water pump station with rooftop vents and exposed utility pipework.
04-water-pump-station.sizeGuidance: Scale from the facility footprint, with pipe inlet/outlet anchors kept independent of decorative crop bounds.

05-elevated-water-tower.description: Elevated water tank on four legs, with a service ladder and central riser.
05-elevated-water-tower.sizeGuidance: Calibrate the leg footprint and tank elevation separately. The overhead footprint must not inherit the tall isometric sprite height.

06-gas-city-gate.description: Fenced gas receiving and regulating station with control cabinets and parallel pipe trains.
06-gas-city-gate.sizeGuidance: Use the fenced station footprint with transmission inlet and distribution outlet anchors. Do not automatically reuse as a smaller district regulator station.

07-bucket-line-truck.description: Electric line truck with a stowed bucket boom, side ladder and cable reel.
07-bucket-line-truck.sizeGuidance: Share road scale with other crew vehicles. Calibrate tire contact and wheelbase, keeping a truck clearly smaller than a house footprint.

08-water-crew-truck-excavator.description: Water crew service truck and a compact excavator in a parked working-site arrangement.
08-water-crew-truck-excavator.sizeGuidance: This is a composite parked study. Separate the truck and excavator before routing or animating either one; do not drive the whole paired sheet down a road.

09-gas-service-truck.description: Gas service truck with fixed tool lockers, pipe storage and safety equipment.
09-gas-service-truck.sizeGuidance: Use the same vehicle scale and tire-contact convention as the electric line truck and meter van.

10-meter-technician-van.description: Compact meter service van with a roof ladder and a consistent sliding-door side.
10-meter-technician-van.sizeGuidance: Smaller than the heavy utility trucks. Field, relight and drive-by AMR roles require explicit job bindings and distinct role markings if this design is reused.

11-residential-electric-ami-meter.description: Residential electric AMI meter and weatherproof wall cabinet, drawn as a mountable assembly.
bindings: service points and registers linked to meter ID
11-residential-electric-ami-meter.sizeGuidance: A small wall attachment. Scale from its mounting face and make it legible through close zoom or a detail panel; never use house-sized sheet scaling.

12-residential-diaphragm-gas-meter.description: Residential diaphragm gas meter with a service regulator and connected pipe assembly.
bindings: gas meter node meterClass: 250 CFH diaphragm
12-residential-diaphragm-gas-meter.sizeGuidance: A small house-side assembly with explicit inlet/outlet ports and a wall-side orientation. Commercial rotary sets require a separate asset family.
